enonce_markdown: Which part of the eye controls the amount of light that enters it?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Each part of the eye has one main job: some bend light, some control it and some detect it.

### Solution

The iris is a coloured ring of muscle which changes the size of the pupil and so controls how much light enters. The cornea and lens refract light, and the retina detects it.

**Answer: C.**

enonce_markdown: Which part of the eye contains the light-sensitive cells (rods and cones)?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Light-sensitive cells change light into nerve impulses; ask which layer is at the back of the eye.

### Solution

The retina is the innermost layer at the back of the eye and contains rods (dim light) and cones (colour, bright light). The choroid contains blood vessels and pigment, the sclera is the tough outer coat and the cornea is the clear front part.

**Answer: D.**

enonce_markdown: Nkeng walks out of a dark room into bright sunshine. What happens to his pupils, and how?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

The iris has circular and radial muscles which work in opposite ways. The pupil gets smaller to protect the retina in bright light.

### Solution

In bright light the circular muscles of the iris contract and the radial muscles relax. The pupil becomes smaller (constricts), reducing the light entering the eye and protecting the retina from damage.

**Answer: B.**

choix.texte: They get smaller because the radial muscles of the iris contract
They get smaller because the circular muscles of the iris contract
They get larger because the circular muscles of the iris contract
They get larger because the radial muscles of the iris relax

enonce_markdown: A student looks up from the blackboard to read the book on her desk. Which row describes the changes in the eye that let her see the book clearly?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Accommodation: to focus a near object, the lens must become thicker (more convex) and bend light more.

### Solution

For a near object, the ciliary muscles contract, so the tension on the suspensory ligaments falls (they slacken). The lens, which is elastic, becomes thicker and more rounded and so bends light more strongly. Looking at a distant object needs the opposite changes.

**Answer: A.**

choix.texte: Ciliary muscles contract; suspensory ligaments slacken; lens becomes thicker
Ciliary muscles relax; suspensory ligaments pull tight; lens becomes thinner
Ciliary muscles contract; suspensory ligaments pull tight; lens becomes thinner
Ciliary muscles relax; suspensory ligaments slacken; lens becomes thicker

enonce_markdown: State **one** function of each of the following parts of the human eye: (i) cornea, (ii) choroid, (iii) optic nerve, (iv) vitreous humour. *(4 marks)*
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Give the job of each part in a short phrase: what it does for light or for the eye.

### Solution

(i) **Cornea**: a transparent window at the front that lets light in and bends (refracts) it.

(ii) **Choroid**: contains blood vessels that supply the retina, and its dark pigment absorbs stray light and prevents reflection inside the eye.

(iii) **Optic nerve**: carries nerve impulses from the retina to the brain.

(iv) **Vitreous humour**: a jelly-like fluid which keeps the shape of the eyeball and supports the retina and lens.

enonce_markdown: When Mbah enters a cinema from the bright street, he cannot see anything, but after a few minutes he can see the seats. Explain the changes in the eye which allow him to see in the dim light. *(4 marks)*
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Compare how much light reaches the retina at first and later. Consider the iris and the cells in the retina.

### Solution

In dim light the radial muscles of the iris contract and the circular muscles relax, so the pupil dilates (becomes larger). More light can enter the eye and reach the retina. The rod cells of the retina, which are sensitive to dim light, become more sensitive after some minutes in the dark. The impulses from the rods go through the optic nerve to the brain, so he can see the seats.
